title: Geotechnical Testing Labs
tagline: Find accredited geotechnical and materials testing labs by test method, turnaround and region
problem: Contractors and engineers need soil borings, compaction testing, concrete cylinders and asphalt tests from labs accredited for specific ASTM/AASHTO methods, often required by DOTs and project specs. Accreditation lookups are split between AASHTO re:source, A2LA and state DOT approved-lab lists, and turnaround and field-tech availability is learned by phone. A rejected lab report can stall a pour or a pay application.
solution: A test-method-aware directory of geotechnical and construction materials testing labs. Accreditation data from AASHTO re:source, A2LA and state DOT qualified-lab lists is parsed into method-level rows (e.g. ASTM D1557, AASHTO T 99, C39). Users enter required test methods and a project location to get labs within mobilization distance that hold those accreditations, with turnaround and field-tech availability. Contractors issue RFQs, and engineers can confirm a lab's accreditation for a spec submittal in one click, with dated proof.
target_audience: General and site contractors; civil and geotechnical engineers; developers; DOT and municipal project managers
pricing: Free search; labs $199/mo profile, $20 per RFQ; contractors $49/mo submittal-proof exports
platform_distribution: Google SEO ("compaction testing [city]"); ASCE Geo-Institute and ACEC member networks; contractor associations
competitors: AASHTO re:source lab directory; A2LA directory; state DOT approved-lab lists; The Blue Book
competitor_gap: Accreditation directories are siloed and do not show turnaround, mobilization radius or RFQs
demand_evidence: AASHTO re:source and A2LA both run accreditation programs for construction materials labs, and ASTM methods are written into project specs, so method-level accreditation checks are routine.
unique_data_capture: Method-level accreditation rows across AASHTO re:source, A2LA and DOT lists, joined to quoted turnaround and mobilization radius per lab
commoditization_risk: Low: requires a maintained cross-body accreditation dataset
regulatory_notes: State DOT lab qualification rules; the platform does not certify results
mvp_features: Method-level accreditation search; project-radius filter; RFQ routing; submittal proof export; accreditation change alerts
review_notes: Depends on reliably parsing accreditation scopes; the same parsing engine as DIR-235 could serve both.
score_justification: L4 LLM parses accreditation scopes by method; E3 data pipeline 4-6 wks; A3 spec-driven recurring need; P3 contractor/engineer networks; M4 method-level accreditation + turnaround data; W4 testing is a paid line item on every project
